findings.description: When GitHub's head is unreadable (`review.head === undefined`), `isPinned` is false, so an OPEN PR now ends the wait with "the head moved off <pin>" and points to `pup merge <id> --pr`. That re-gate refuses an unreadable head. Before this delta the wait kept waiting, and `land.service.ts:97` treats an unreadable head as not moved (`pr.head !== undefined && pr.head !== sha`). In practice `headRefOid` is non-null, so this only matters for a malformed answer. Keeping the old behaviour, treating an unreadable head as one more wait, would match land's reading.

Any GitHub account can stall `pup ci wait` until its timeout. Posting 100 PR comments after the bot's `claude-review` status sets `hasPreviousPage` with every comment on the page newer than the status, so `isRereviewAsked` reads true. The wait then times out with "a review of <head> asked by comment after its status" and "Re-run `pup ci wait <id>`". This fails closed: no false verdict, no new next step, bounded by `timeoutMs`. But it contradicts decision 86's "Another account's comment starts no run, so it holds nothing". The waiting text also tells the conductor an ask happened when none did. On a public repo the flood can be repeated on every re-run.

An owner `@claude review` comment made while another review run is still in flight is not detected. The workflow's job concurrency queues the comment's run, and the in-flight run's poster then sets a `claude-review` status newer than the comment. So `isRereviewAsked` reads false, and `pup ci wait` can finish on the first run's verdict while the queued re-review is still pending. The window is small and the first run reviewed the same head.

The change turns the existing `FORMAT_CHARS` regex into an exported constant of `fix-round.service.ts`, and `ci-wait.service.ts` now imports it from there. That makes one service import another service's internal constant. `general.md` §No hardcoded values puts constants in the area's `*.constants.ts`. Move it into a constants file both services import, such as `merge-gate.constants.ts`, or next to `sanitizeReason` in `capability.utils.ts`, with a shared strip-then-sanitize helper.

Two sources of truth for one review verdict. `PullRequestReview` gains the derived boolean `isRereviewAsked`, and the digest in `ci-wait` then decides on it separately from the raw fields. `reviewStatusOn` now returns an internal `setAt`, and the caller immediately re-maps the result with `status && { state, description }` to drop that field and keep the public shape. This is the only place `setAt` is used, so the exported type and the internal type now differ by one field.

`isReviewAskedSince` hardcodes the workflow's trigger (`/@claude review/i`, `authorAssociation === 'OWNER'`). The comment cites `.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml` for the rules, but nothing ties the code to that file, so a workflow edit leaves the client wrong without any signal. A check that the repo's own `.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml` still contains the trigger string would be cheap protection.

The `reason` closure reads the shared module-level sticky `VERDICT.lastIndex` lazily. It is correct only because it is called right after a successful `exec` that matched a verdict word. A failed `exec` resets `lastIndex` to 0, so any later reorder or deferred call would silently slice from the wrong offset (Mysterious Name / hidden temporal coupling).

The three-way branch inside the nested summary/clause/id loop has no comment on its precedence. When an id opens a clause, the branch overwrites any earlier answer for that id, even with `undefined`. A mid-clause id only sets an answer if it is colon-form, and otherwise only records a first sighting. The `named.has(id)` guard is what makes a mention inside a reason never downgrade an answer, and nothing says so. The loop is also three levels deep, with an `undefined` map value doubling as 'named but unanswered'.

The test builds a summary of about 1 MB, but `threadAnswers` reads only `SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS` (64 KiB) of it. Even a per-mention algorithm would finish 64 KiB within the 2 s bound, so the test cannot catch the regression it names. The doc line it backs ("reads a megabyte of mentions within a time bound") overstates it the same way.

The sentence still says answers are taken "by its last mention in the newest summary naming it". The text added later in that sentence, and `threadAnswers`, say a mention inside a reason neither answers nor cancels within its summary. The rule is now "by its last answer".

Two lines this delta edits in decision 90 run well past the file's ~100-column wrap, because new text was spliced onto old lines without re-wrapping: L4864 ends with "One GraphQL read (`readThreadAnswers`, pinned", and L4974 is "reads a megabyte of mentions within a time bound, posts nothing again on a second run, gives up within its budget on a gh". Re-wrap both paragraphs.

process_issues.description: Both maintainability instances skipped the test files in their slices (ci-wait.test.ts, github-client.test.ts, fix-round.test.ts), so the delta's tests got no maintainability coverage.
The conventions reviewer did not read the test files or docs/09-decisions.md, so its coverage of the delta was partial.
